CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old female with history of congestive heart failure and kidney stones who presents for abnormal lab finding. Patient reports fatigue and dizziness over the past couple of months. She notes feeling worn out with activities such as walking a mile or going to work that previously did not cause fatigue. Denies syncope, weight loss, or loss of appetite. Regarding gastrointestinal symptoms, patient denies current blood in stools, though reports blood in stools approximately 3 years ago that led to colonoscopy revealing mild diverticulosis. Since that time, no further gastrointestinal issues. Denies dark, tarry, or black stools. Denies heavy menstrual bleeding. Regarding congestive heart failure, patient acknowledges recent difficulty adhering to salt-restricted diet while traveling to Vermont and consuming fast food including cheeseburgers at McDonald's. Notes some swelling in legs but states it is not severe. Denies shortness of breath or problems lying flat at night. Regarding kidney stones, which patient experienced a couple years ago, denies recent flare-ups, back pain, flank pain, or blood in urine. Additionally, patient reports seasonal allergies with nasal congestion.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Nurse completed review of systems at time of presentation. Patient endorses dizziness and fatigue. Also endorses nasal congestion from seasonal allergies. Denies fever, chills, sore throat, or cough.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congestive heart failure
Kidney stones
Diverticulosis

MEDICATIONS
Toprol 50 mg daily
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Lasix 40 mg once daily (newly initiated)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent travel to Vermont. Employed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure and heart rate normal.
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur noted on heart examination (previously appreciated).
Extremities: Trace to 1+ pitting edema in ankles.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin: 8.2 g/dL (low)
Echocardiogram from approximately 6 months prior: Ejection fraction 45%, moderate mitral regurgitation

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Anemia: Order anemia profile labs to determine type of anemia. Refer to gastroenterology for evaluation including endoscopy and colonoscopy.

Congestive heart failure: Fluid retention noted on physical examination. Start lasix 40 mg once daily. Continue toprol 50 mg daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Reinforce dietary salt restriction. Patient to weigh herself daily and report any weight gain to clinic.

Kidney stones: Currently stable. Continue dietary management and hydration.
